newsitem.title: USA: Rig count rise 17 to 858 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Rig count rise 17 to 858 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 858 as of Dec. 23, up 17 from the prior week and 96 above the year-ago total of 762, oilfield services company Baker Hughes Inc. said Monday.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by 12 to 717, while rigs working offshore rose five to 119. The number of rigs active in inland waters remained unchanged at 22.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in Texas, which showed a decrease of 10 and Oklahoma, which showed an increase of 13. Louisiana rose by one.

A total of 360 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down four from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by 21 to 496, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at two.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 14 to 405 vs. 287 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, consultant Offshore Data Services said there were 161 rigs under contract in the Gulf of Mexico as of Dec. 20, down two from the prior week.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 179, was 89.9 percent.
